c.tagline: Vietnam's former imperial capital — a walled Citadel, royal tombs, and refined court cuisine on the Perfume River.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis (Mai Linh, Vinasun) are reliable, but Grab and the electric Xanh SM are usually cheaper and remove any haggling; cyclos (pedicabs) are a slow, scenic way to see the old town for an agreed price.

emergency.note: 114 reaches the fire service. Operators may have limited English; hotel reception can help relay an emergency.

hood_landmark.Vỹ Dạ: Vy Da ward Hue Perfume River

avoid.reason: Watch for cyclo and taxi overcharging around the Citadel and Dong Ba Market, and occasional bag-snatching from motorbikes at night.

hood_desc: The south-bank city center facing the Perfume River, where most of Hue's hotels, restaurants, cafes and travel agencies cluster along Le Loi and Hung Vuong; the most convenient, walkable base for first-timers, a short bridge crossing from the Citadel.

The walled old imperial city on the north bank, enclosing the UNESCO-listed Citadel and Forbidden Purple City; a tranquil, historic quarter of low lanes, moats and small guesthouses, ideal for culture lovers who want to sleep beside the royal relics.

A riverside residential ward east of the center, famous among locals for garden houses and some of Hue's best street food; a quiet, authentic, off-the-tourist-track base for foodies and slower travelers.

A leafy stretch along the Perfume River west of the Citadel toward Thien Mu Pagoda, dotted with garden villas and upscale riverside resorts; a calm, scenic area for a restful, resort-style stay near the pagodas and royal tombs.
lodging: Spatel d'Annam - Imperial Boutique Spa & Hotel

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not potable.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 5:00 AM to 6:00 PM; there is no late-night public transit, so Grab, Xanh SM, taxis and cyclos cover the evenings.
transit.note: Hue has no metro or tram; a small network of public city buses serves the main routes, but most visitors get around by Grab, Xanh SM (electric taxis/bikes), metered taxis, cyclos and rented motorbikes, and by dragon-boat on the Perfume River.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the conductor (around 7,000-15,000 VND); there is no city-wide smartcard, and ride-hailing apps are paid in-app or in cash.

bus: Hue Southern (An Cuu) and Northern (An Hoa) bus stations
Open-tour and sleeper buses to Hoi An, Da Nang, Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City
train: Hue Railway Station (North-South Reunification line to Da Nang, Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City)

transit.m: Metered taxi or Grab to the city center (25-30 min)
Airport shuttle bus to central Hue (No. 20 Hanoi St), every ~30 min

tip.r: Tipping is not expected; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service at tourist-facing restaurants, and tipping tour guides, drivers and spa staff, is appreciated.

food.name: Bun bo Hue
food.desc: The city's famous noodle soup: thick round rice noodles in a beef-bone and pork-trotter broth spiked with lemongrass and shrimp-paste chilli oil.

places.name: Bun Bo Hue Ba Gai
places.note: Well-balanced, properly spicy broth with crab cake and beef shank; a long-standing local name.

places.name: Quan Cam
places.note: Super-casual local eatery with a queue most mornings; sells out by mid-morning.

places.name: Dong Ba Market noodle stalls
places.area: Dong Ba, by the Perfume River
places.note: Market stalls serving the breakfast bowl locals eat, from around 6am.

food.name: Banh beo, nam and loc
food.desc: The Hue rice-cake trio: banh beo water-fern discs with dried shrimp, banh nam steamed flat in banana leaf, and chewy tapioca banh bot loc around a whole prawn.

places.name: Hang Me Me
places.note: The standard address for the full rice-cake platter; also banh cuon and banh ram it.

places.name: Ba Do
places.note: Long-time favourite with Vietnamese visitors for banh beo, banh nam and banh loc.

places.name: Madam Thu Restaurant
places.area: Vo Thi Sau, near the walking street
places.note: Sampler platter of Hue specialties in one sitting; useful if you have one evening.

food.name: Com hen
food.desc: Cold rice topped with tiny stir-fried river clams, crackling, peanuts, herbs, star fruit and fermented shrimp paste, with a bowl of clam broth alongside.

places.name: Com Hen Hoa Dong
places.note: On the sandbar island the clams come from; the definitive version, eaten by locals.

places.name: Quan Com Hen Ba Cam
places.note: Neighbourhood shop doing com hen and bun hen from early morning at street prices.

places.name: Dong Ba Market
places.note: Market stalls serving both the rice and the noodle version; ask for less shrimp paste if new to it.

food.name: Banh khoai
food.desc: Hue's small, thick, crisp turmeric pancake stuffed with pork and prawn, folded over beansprouts and dipped in a thick fermented-soybean and peanut sauce.

places.name: Lac Thien
places.area: Dinh Tien Hoang, near the Citadel
places.note: Institution run by a deaf family for decades; the banh khoai everyone is sent to.

places.name: Quan Hanh
places.note: Reliable, tourist-friendly kitchen doing banh khoai, nem lui and banh loc all at once.

places.name: Ba Hong
places.note: Small local shop frying pancakes to order; go early evening before the batter runs out.

food.name: Nem lui
food.desc: Seasoned pork paste moulded onto lemongrass stalks and grilled over coals, then rolled at the table in rice paper with herbs and dipped in thick peanut sauce.

places.name: Quan Hanh
places.note: Best-known address for the full DIY roll-your-own spread; staff will demonstrate.

places.name: Tai Phu
places.note: Local grill house where the skewers come off the coals continuously all evening.

places.name: Madam Thu Restaurant
places.note: Included on the Hue sampler platter; two central branches, open until 10.30pm.

food.name: Che Hue
food.desc: Hue makes dozens of che sweet soups, the strangest being che bot loc boc heo - candied pork fat sealed inside a tapioca pearl in sweet ginger syrup.

places.name: Che Hem
places.note: Alleyway che shop with a long list of varieties; the local late-night dessert stop.

places.name: Dong Ba Market sweet stalls
places.note: Rows of che vendors in the market's food section, each with its own specialty.

places.name: Che Mo Ton Dich
places.note: Old family che shop near the Citadel serving the traditional Hue varieties.

food.name: Tra sen (lotus tea)
food.desc: Green tea scented with lotus from the Citadel moats and Tinh Tam lake, a refinement of the Nguyen court. Served in small cups in the city's garden houses.

places.name: Tinh Gia Vien
places.note: Garden restaurant in an old royal-style house serving imperial-style tea and set menus.

places.name: Ancient Hue Garden Houses
places.note: Restored traditional wooden garden compound; tea service in the old Hue manner.

places.name: Dong Ba Market tea sellers
places.note: Buy loose lotus tea by weight; vendors let you smell before you commit.

food.name: Ca phe muoi
food.desc: Salt coffee - invented in Hue. Robusta drips onto salted fermented cream, and you stir it through so the salt cuts the bitterness. Now copied nationwide.

places.name: Ca Phe Muoi
places.note: The original salt-coffee shop where the drink was created; tiny, cash only, always busy.

places.name: Ca Phe Muoi riverside branch
places.note: Same family, easier to reach from the hotel strip, with river-facing seats.

places.name: Madam Thu Restaurant
places.note: Serves salt coffee alongside the food platter if you would rather do both at once.

landmarks: Imperial City (Hue Citadel)
The UNESCO-listed walled seat of the Nguyen emperors, a moated complex of ceremonial gates, throne halls and the storied Forbidden Purple City.
Thien Mu Pagoda
Hue's seven-tiered riverside icon, a 17th-century pagoda whose octagonal tower and monastic gardens overlook the slow-drifting Perfume River.
Tomb of Khai Dinh
A theatrical hillside mausoleum blending European baroque with Vietnamese dragon mosaics, its blackened concrete exterior hiding a dazzling glass-inlaid interior.
Tomb of Tu Duc
A romantic lakeside retreat of frangipani groves and pleasure pavilions where the poet-emperor relaxed, wrote verse and planned his own elegant burial.
Tomb of Minh Mang
The most majestic Nguyen tomb, a solemn axis of gates, courtyards and crescent lakes expressing Confucian harmony in a pine-forested setting.
Perfume River (Song Huong)
Hue's lifeblood, best savored on a dragon boat drifting past pagodas and royal tombs as sunset gilds the water.
Dong Ba Market
The city's century-old market, a fragrant crush of conical hats, bun bo Hue stalls and river produce beside Trang Tien Bridge.
Trang Tien Bridge
A graceful Gustave Eiffel-era steel bridge across the Perfume River that glows in shifting rainbow colors after dark.
An Dinh Palace
An ornate early-20th-century royal residence fusing Vietnamese and European styles, once home to Emperor Bao Dai and now a gorgeously restored film-set favorite.
Thanh Toan Tile-Roofed Bridge
A charming 18th-century Japanese-style covered bridge in a rice-farming village outside Hue, perfect for a countryside cycling excursion.

train.note: Hue Railway Station sits on the North-South Reunification line. SE and TN trains run south to Da Nang (~2.5 hr over the spectacular Hai Van Pass), on to Ho Chi Minh City (~18-19 hr), and north to Hanoi (~13-14 hr). There are no international rail services from Vietnam.

intl.to: Savannakhet & Vientiane (Laos) - via the Lao Bao border
intl.op: cross-border coach operators — tickets at the bus station or through local agents

bus.note: Open-tour buses and shuttles run frequently south to Da Nang and Hoi An (~2.5-3 hr over the Hai Van Pass) and north toward the DMZ, while sleeper coaches connect Hue with Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City overnight. Some cross-border coaches run to Savannakhet and Vientiane in Laos via the Lao Bao border.

ferry.note: Hue has no scheduled passenger ferries; the Perfume River is plied by tourist dragon-boats running upriver to Thien Mu Pagoda and the royal tombs.

half.name: Tam Giang Lagoon
half.blurb: Southeast Asia's largest lagoon, famous for fishing villages, floating nets and spectacular sunsets.

full.name: Hai Van Pass
full.blurb: Vietnam's dramatic coastal mountain pass on the old Hue-Da Nang highway, with sweeping views over Lang Co Lagoon and the East Sea.

full.name: DMZ & Vinh Moc Tunnels
full.blurb: Vietnam's former Demilitarized Zone on the Ben Hai River, with the wartime tunnel village of Vinh Moc dug into the coastal cliffs (about 2h30 by road).

laundry.pay: cash; MoMo or bank transfer; note-fed tokens at laundromats
laundry.note: Per-kilo drop-off dominates; US-style laundromats are uncommon
